Despite these positive indicators, the market has left the company with a negligible market capitalisation of ₹ 5.56 Cr [E2]. The company is currently destroying value at an alarming rate, evidenced by a Return on Assets (ROA) of -33.9%, a figure that drastically underperforms the sector benchmark of 4.93% [E7]. This operational inefficiency is further reflected in the company’s inability to generate consistent profit growth, as evidenced by a -5% compounded profit growth rate over the last three years and 0% growth over the trailing twelve months [E13, E14]. Investors are also denied any immediate return on their capital, as the dividend yield stands at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: [E8, E15, E44]. While the company shows some signs of recent profit growth outperforming price growth, these metrics cannot mask the underlying structural instability of a business operating with negative equity [E1, E38].

The bear’s focus on negative book value [E1] ignores the reality that the company is currently generating a robust Return on Equity of 21.9%, which significantly outperforms the sector benchmark of 10.46% [E8]. While the bear highlights ROA [E7], it overlooks the fact that the company is currently in a phase of accelerating earnings growth [E44]. The claim that the business is stagnant is contradicted by the fact that profit growth is now outpacing price growth, signaling that the company is beginning to outperform market expectations [E38]. Although the bear cites a lack of dividends [E3], the long-term investor has been rewarded with a 10-year compounded share price growth of 18% [E15]. Conceded: [E1, E3, E7, E13, E14]. Ultimately, the bear’s reliance on static balance sheet metrics fails to account for the positive momentum in earnings and share price performance [E15, E44].
